definition: Brown-coloured nymphs (immature, wingless insect stages) seen on the plant, usually at the base of tillers or on lower leaf sheaths.
scope_note: Records the insect, not plant damage. Colour-specific variant of Nymphs_Present; use Nymphs_Present when colour is not reported.

definition: Yellow- or pale-coloured nymphs (immature, wingless insect stages) seen on the plant.
scope_note: Colour-specific variant of Nymphs_Present; use Nymphs_Present when colour is not reported.

definition: Insect eggs or egg masses deposited on leaf blades or leaf sheaths and visible without dissection.
scope_note: Excludes nematode egg masses inside root tissue, which are not field-visible.

definition: Loss of a large part of the leaf blade to insect feeding, leaving much of the blade missing.
scope_note: Use Leaf_Chewing_Damage for localized notches or holes.

definition: Panicles or panicle branches cut off at the neck or peduncle by insect feeding.
scope_note: A mechanical cut, not a lesion; use Panicle_Neck_Rot when the neck is necrotic and the panicle remains attached.

definition: Irregular notches, holes or ragged margins on the leaf blade caused by the mouthparts of chewing insects.
scope_note: Localized feeding marks; use Broad_Leaf_Damage when most of the blade is consumed.

definition: Galls (swellings) at the root tips that bend the tip into a curved, hook-like shape.
scope_note: Use Root_Knot_Swelling for galls not described as hooked. Nematode cysts attached to the root surface are not galls.

definition: Round or spindle-shaped swellings (galls) formed along the root axis, not specifically at a hooked tip.
scope_note: Galls are swellings of root tissue; nematode cysts (e.g. Heterodera) are external bodies attached to the root and are not galls.

definition: Roots that are bent, twisted, shortened or thickened in shape beyond discrete galls.
scope_note: Use Discolored_Roots for a colour change without a change in shape.

definition: Small discrete spots or lesions of dead tissue (brown, grey or black) on the plant, of any shape.
scope_note: General lesion term. Use Diamond_Shaped_Lesions for spindle or diamond lesions with a grey centre, and Brown_Streaks for narrow lesions running along the veins.

definition: Pale green to yellow colour (chlorosis) over whole leaf blades on one or more leaves.
scope_note: Use Plant_Yellowing when the whole plant is uniformly yellow, Yellowing_Leaf_Tips when yellowing starts at the tip, Orange_Leaf_Discoloration for a yellow-orange hue, and Leaf_Mottling for a patchy pattern.

definition: Plants noticeably shorter than healthy plants of the same age and cultivar.
scope_note: Use Severe_Stunting when the source describes marked dwarfing.

definition: Insect excrement and boring debris found inside the stem or at entry holes in the culm.
scope_note: Direct evidence of a stem-boring insect.

definition: Small entry or exit holes in the culm or leaf sheath made by stem-boring larvae.
At the vegetative stage, not only in seedlings, the central shoot of a tiller turns yellow-brown and dries while the outer leaves stay green; caused by stem borers.
scope_note: The identifier's 'Seedling' suffix is historical; the term applies to any vegetative tiller. The reproductive-stage counterpart is Whitehead_Empty_Panicles.

definition: Affected tillers or central shoots come away with little resistance when pulled, because the stem base is severed internally.
Panicles that emerge white or straw-coloured, stay erect and carry mostly unfilled grains.
scope_note: Records the whole panicle as empty, whatever the cause (stem borer, virus-induced poor heading). Use Empty_Grains when only some grains are unfilled.

definition: Immature, wingless stages of insects observed on the plant, colour not specified.
Adult insects observed feeding or resting on the plant.
scope_note: Use Brown_Planthopper_Present or Green_Leafhopper_Present when the insect is identified as a virus vector.

definition: Small silvery, pale or drying spots on the leaf margins or tips caused by sap-sucking insects such as thrips, often with leaf rolling.
scope_note: Record only when the insect cause is reported, to keep it apart from disease lesions on the leaf margin.

definition: Panicles whose spikelets or grains are discoloured, shrivelled or decaying.
scope_note: Use Panicle_Neck_Rot when the lesion is at the panicle neck node.

definition: Damage scattered irregularly across the field rather than in patches, rows or foci.
scope_note: Field-level context, not a sign on a single plant.

definition: Yellowing confined to discrete patches on individual leaves while the rest of the blade stays green.
scope_note: Use Yellowing_Leaves when whole blades are yellow.

definition: Spikelets that are unfilled or only partly filled (chaffy) at grain filling or maturity.
scope_note: Use Whitehead_Empty_Panicles when the whole panicle is white and empty.

definition: Yellowing that affects the whole plant or nearly all of its leaves uniformly.
scope_note: Use Yellowing_Leaves when yellowing is reported for leaves rather than the whole plant.

definition: Plants yellow, then brown and dry from the base upward after heavy planthopper feeding, looking burnt.
scope_note: Insect-caused; use Leaf_Desiccation for drying of leaves from disease.

definition: Circular or oval patches of dried, collapsed plants within the field that enlarge outward.
scope_note: Field-level context.

definition: Small dark or black spots at the feeding sites of piercing-sucking insects on stems, sheaths or grains.
Lesions that extend along the veins, especially the midrib, with a wavy yellow border.
scope_note: The identifier suggests yellowing of the veins themselves; the term denotes lesion spread along them.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: Yellow lesions or yellow bands extending along the margins of the leaf blade.
scope_note: The identifier suggests general yellowing, but the term denotes marginal lesions only; use Yellowing_Leaves for whole yellow blades and Yellowing_Leaf_Tips when yellowing starts at the tip.

definition: Yellowing that begins at the leaf tip and progresses toward the base.
scope_note: Use Whitened_Leaf_Tips when the tip turns white, and Orange_Leaf_Discoloration when the colour is yellow-orange.

definition: The number of affected plants or the affected area is reported to increase quickly across the field.
scope_note: Field-level context, often reported after storms or heavy rain.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: Grains replaced by velvety spore balls larger than a normal grain, yellow-orange to green or yellowish-green and not yet blackened.
scope_note: Also use when the colour is reported only as 'green', without 'dark' or 'black'; use Blackened_Grain_Balls once the balls are dark green to black.

label_en: dark green to black spore balls
definition: Mature spore balls replacing grains that have turned dark olive-green to greenish-black.
scope_note: Mature stage of the balls described in Rusty_Grain_Balls.

definition: Disease occurs during or after a period of frequent rain and high humidity, especially around flowering.
scope_note: Field-level context.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: Symptoms affect plants throughout large continuous areas of the field rather than isolated plants or patches.
scope_note: Field-level context.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: Only a few spikelets per panicle are affected, whatever the symptom, for example a few spore balls per panicle.
scope_note: Early lesions confined to the glumes are one instance, not a requirement.

label_en: symptom onset between flowering and milky stage
label_id: muncul pada fase berbunga hingga masak susu
definition: Symptoms are first seen between flowering and the milky grain stage.
scope_note: Crop-stage context. The identifier's 'vulnerability' is historical: for false smut, infection itself occurs at booting, before symptoms appear.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: Brown to black necrotic lesion on the panicle neck node; the panicle may break over or stay partly unfilled.
scope_note: Panicle still attached; use Severed_Panicles when it has been cut off.

definition: Spindle- or diamond-shaped leaf lesions with a grey or whitish centre and a brown margin.
scope_note: More specific than Necrotic_Spots; record Necrotic_Spots as well only if spots of a different shape are also reported.

definition: Symptomatic or dying seedlings in the nursery bed or soon after transplanting.
scope_note: Crop-stage context.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: Brown planthoppers (Nilaparvata lugens) observed on the plant.
scope_note: Recorded as a virus vector sighting.

definition: Marked dwarfing: plants described as severely stunted or dwarf compared with healthy neighbours.
scope_note: Use Stunted_Growth when stunting is reported without emphasis on severity.

definition: Plants produce no panicles, or only a few small panicles, when healthy plants have headed.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: Green leafhoppers (Nephotettix spp., especially N. virescens) observed on the plant.
scope_note: Recorded as a virus vector sighting.

definition: Dark green, translucent, water-soaked spots or stripes on the leaf, usually an early stage of lesion development.
scope_note: Record even when later-stage lesions are also described.

definition: Droplets or dried beads of yellowish bacterial exudate on the surface of lesions.
source_citation: Ou, S.H. (1985). Rice Diseases, 2nd edition. Commonwealth Mycological Institute, Kew, Surrey, UK.

definition: An irregular pattern of light green or yellow and normal green areas on the leaf blade.
scope_note: Use Yellowing_Leaves for uniform yellowing and Chlorotic_Streaks for narrow stripes.

definition: Yellowing of the tissue between the leaf veins while the veins stay green, reported explicitly as an interveinal pattern.
scope_note: Translucent tissue in bacterial lesions is excluded: use Chlorotic_Streaks or Water_Soaked_Lesions.

definition: Grains or hulls with brown, black, reddish or other abnormal spots or colour.
Spots, blotches or rot on the leaf sheath rather than the leaf blade.
Dark lesions or rot on the culm or at the stem base, sometimes with tiller decay or lodging.
An abnormally high number of tillers per hill, giving a bushy or grassy appearance.
Yellow-orange to orange colouring of the leaf, usually starting from the tip.
scope_note: Use Yellowing_Leaves when the colour is reported only as yellow.

definition: Leaves dry out and turn straw-coloured or brown over most of the blade.
scope_note: Disease-related drying; use Hopperburn_Drying for drying caused by planthopper feeding.

definition: Narrow yellow, pale or translucent stripes running parallel to the veins.
scope_note: On parallel-veined rice leaves use this term for every striped chlorosis pattern; use Interveinal_Chlorosis only when the source explicitly reports an interveinal pattern.

definition: Narrow brown necrotic streaks parallel to the veins on the leaf blade or sheath, much longer than they are wide.
scope_note: Use Necrotic_Spots for discrete spots without an elongated pattern along the veins.

definition: Leaves turn whitish, greyish-white or pale straw-coloured (bleached).
The apical part of the leaf turns white and may later become brown or twisted.
scope_note: Use Yellowing_Leaf_Tips when the tip turns yellow.

definition: Leaves droop or roll from loss of turgor.
scope_note: Premature death of the plant is a separate observation and is not part of this term; the vocabulary has no term for it yet.

definition: Roots that are brown or black instead of white or cream.
scope_note: Colour change only; use Deformed_Roots or the root gall terms for changes in shape.

definition: Fungal disease of rice caused by Pyricularia oryzae (teleomorph Magnaporthe oryzae), affecting leaves, nodes and panicle necks.

Bacterial disease of rice caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae: water-soaked lesions start at the leaf tip or margins and extend toward the base with a wavy yellow border, often with bacterial exudate; at the seedling stage it causes wilting (kresek).
scope_note: Distinguish from bacterial leaf streak (X. oryzae pv. oryzicola), which forms narrow translucent streaks between the veins.

definition: Fungal disease of rice caused by Ustilaginoidea virens, in which individual grains are replaced by spore balls.
Viral disease of rice caused by rice grassy stunt virus (genus Tenuivirus), transmitted by the brown planthopper.

Tungro disease, caused by joint infection with rice tungro bacilliform virus (Tungrovirus) and rice tungro spherical virus (Waikavirus), transmitted by green leafhoppers, mainly Nephotettix virescens.
scope_note: The identifier names a single virus; the disease involves two.

definition: Rice root-knot nematode Meloidogyne graminicola, which forms hook-shaped galls at the root tips.
scope_note: In the literature the common name 'rice root nematode' usually denotes Hirschmanniella oryzae. This individual is aligned to M. graminicola (AGROVOC c_31070) and its rules use root-gall signs.
